chunks: And from him from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from him (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no prayer for the two Eids except with an Imam; so if you pray alone, there is no harm."
And from him from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
I asked him about the prayer on the day of al-Fitr and al-Adha, so he said: "It is not a prayer except with an Imam."
ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to have an Imam for Eid prayers, or can one pray alone?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic status of Eid prayers by distinguishing between the ideal communal performance with an Imam and the validity of individual prayer. The phrase 'la ba'sa' (no blame) indicates that while congregational prayer is preferred for its social and political symbolism of unity, the prayer remains valid even when performed alone, reflecting the Shia view on the flexibility of ritual obligations in the absence of a governing Imam.
